witness_description: Take e(z)=z and c=2. For every complex z with |z|>1, the displayed two-sided magnitude bound holds.
refutation_explanation: Since |z^-1|=1/|z|, the displayed upper bound is 2|z|, so -2|z|<|e(z)|=|z|<2|z|. But e'(z)=1 is not O(z^-1): for any proposed constants C and R, choosing a real z greater than both R and C gives 1>C/|z|.
search_space: All 75 triples (a,k,c) in fixed product order a in (1,-1,2,-2,0), k in (1,0,-1,-2,2), c in (1,2,3), representing e(z)=a*z^k on complex |z|>1; each triple was classified symbolically with exact integer comparisons.
